stories.headline: Copilot code review adds clearer progress and smarter batch suggestions
stories.summary: GitHub updated Copilot code review with a clearer view of review progress, smarter auto-resolution of its own suggestions, and useful commit messages when developers accept suggestions in batches.
stories.why_it_matters: The changes make AI-assisted review easier to follow and reduce friction when turning multiple review suggestions into committed code.
stories.editorial_limitation: Based on GitHub's September 18 product announcement; operational impact will vary by repository and workflow.

what_to_do_now.label: Review the new code-review flow
what_to_do_now.rationale: Check whether clearer progress and batch commit messages reduce review overhead in active repositories.

stories.headline: GitHub schedules selected Copilot model deprecations for October 19
stories.summary: GitHub says selected models will be deprecated across Copilot experiences on October 19, 2026, and points administrators and users toward alternative models available through Copilot model policies and selectors.
stories.why_it_matters: Teams that pin workflows, guidance, or expectations to particular Copilot models need to check model policies and transition plans before the October cutoff.
stories.editorial_limitation: The evidence packet confirms the deprecation and alternative-model guidance but does not reproduce the complete model list.

what_to_do_now.label: Audit Copilot model policies
what_to_do_now.rationale: Identify affected model choices and enable suitable alternatives before the October 19 deprecation date.

visual.title: Copilot model transition
visual.alt_text: Four-step diagram showing current models, policy review, alternative models, and the October 19 transition.

callouts.text: Administrators may need to enable alternative models through policy.

stories.headline: Copilot impact dashboard now exposes feature engagement
stories.summary: GitHub's Copilot impact dashboard now shows how many active users regularly use key Copilot features, helping enterprise administrators see which experiences are broadly adopted and which may need additional enablement.
stories.why_it_matters: AI adoption programs can move beyond license counts and inspect actual feature engagement, creating a better basis for training, rollout, and value-realization decisions.
stories.editorial_limitation: The dashboard measures engagement signals; engagement alone does not establish productivity or business impact.

what_to_do_now.label: Review feature-level engagement
what_to_do_now.rationale: Use engagement data to distinguish widely adopted Copilot experiences from features that need targeted enablement.

nodes.label: Feature usage
nodes.detail: See regular use of key features.

callouts.text: Feature engagement is a stronger adoption signal than licenses alone.

stories.headline: Microsoft codifies lessons from hundreds of internal AI transformation efforts
stories.summary: Microsoft says it has turned lessons from hundreds of internal AI transformation efforts into case studies and a Frontier Playbook designed to scale what worked, learn from failures, and redesign work around AI.
stories.why_it_matters: The account frames enterprise AI transformation as an operating-model problem: capture evidence from real deployments, standardize proven patterns, and continuously redesign workflows rather than treating AI as a one-time tool rollout.
stories.editorial_limitation: This is Microsoft's account of its own transformation and should be read as publisher-authored evidence rather than independent benchmarking.

what_to_do_now.label: Build an internal AI playbook
what_to_do_now.rationale: Capture successful and failed workflow experiments so proven patterns can be reused across teams.

stories.headline: GitHub adds agent skills and customizations to Copilot CLI usage metrics
stories.summary: GitHub expanded Copilot CLI reporting with agentic activity metrics covering skills, custom agents, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins.
stories.why_it_matters: Agent capabilities become easier to govern when organizations can observe which reusable skills and customizations are actually being used instead of treating the agent layer as an opaque configuration surface.
stories.editorial_limitation: Usage metrics show activity, not whether an individual skill or agent produced a correct or valuable outcome.

what_to_do_now.label: Track reusable agent skills
what_to_do_now.rationale: Use the expanded metrics to see which skills, custom agents, MCP servers, commands, and plugins are actually used.

stories.headline: Salesforce explains why long-horizon agents need persistence across sessions
stories.summary: Salesforce describes long-horizon agents as systems that work with users toward goals over time, continue across multiple sessions, and adapt behavior as circumstances change.
stories.why_it_matters: For non-technical users, the important shift is from one-shot task automation to agents that maintain a goal, resume work, and adjust as new information arrives.
stories.editorial_limitation: This is a Salesforce explanatory article, not an independent evaluation of long-horizon agent reliability.

what_to_do_now.label: Define persistent agent goals
what_to_do_now.rationale: For recurring work, specify the goal, checkpoints, changing inputs, and conditions that require human review.

nodes.label: Outcome
nodes.detail: Track progress toward the desired result.

callouts.text: Long-horizon work requires adaptation, not just repeated one-shot prompts.

editorial_takeaway: Today's edition emphasizes operational maturity: clearer AI-assisted engineering workflows, measurable adoption, reusable agent skills, and agents that persist across longer-running work.
